split.plus_en: Courts can review and overturn government decisions and laws; wider standing to petition
split.minus_en: Override clause, limits on standing and on judicial review of government, immigration and demolition decisions
split.statement_en: Courts should be able to overturn government decisions and laws when citizens challenge them, even if this limits what elected governments can do.

split.name_en: Appeals against decisions of public bodies
split.plus_en: Longer appeal periods, reasoned decisions, right to be heard, video documentation of police force
split.minus_en: Fewer duties on public bodies to record, explain or allow appeal of their decisions
split.statement_en: Police, health funds and benefit offices should have to record and explain their decisions so people can challenge them, even at extra cost.

reason: Weight splits into two unrelated blocks of similar size: the heaviest bills (Basic Law: The Government amendments, Basic Law: Entry and Immigration, override clause, standing limits) are about how far courts may review the government (all 'away'), while the many 'toward' bills are everyday administrative accountability: appeal periods for disabled veterans, reasoned answers from health funds, filming police use of skunk water and crowd-dispersal means. The same lists sponsor both kinds (e.g. override and disabled-appeal extension), so one statement mixes the judicial-overhaul axis with a consensual service axis and blurs positions. Tree-protection bill (31) is off-topic.
